meta: Solar calculators for homes: system size, panels, batteries, inverter, charge controller and net billing, using real sun hours for cities in Pakistan.
author: ali-ahmad

sections.h2: Where to start: size the system
p: If you know your units, the solar system size calculator or the solar size from your bill, month by month, gives the kW of panels. If you know your appliances, the five marla house, ten marla house and one kanal house calculators and the one for a mosque or shop size the panels, inverter and battery together.

For one part at a time: the solar panel wattage calculator for the panels, the inverter size calculator for the inverter, the solar battery size calculator for the battery and the charge controller size calculator for an off-grid controller. A home with no grid at all needs the off-grid solar calculator, which also checks the weakest month. For single loads, see how many panels run an AC, the tubewell solar calculator and the solar panel for a twelve-volt battery.

p: Prices come from dated dealer and installer lists: the solar panel price per watt and per panel, the solar system price for whole systems, and the solar quote checker to test a quote against them. New grid connections are on net billing: the net billing calculator shows the bill with solar, and the net billing guide explains the rules.

The solar forecast for tomorrow estimates the next day's output for your city, the cleaning loss calculator shows what dust is costing, and the battery autonomy calculator how many cloudy days the battery covers.

faq.q: What size solar system do I need?
faq.a: Divide the units you use a day by the units one kW of panels makes a day in your city, then round up to whole panels. The solar system size calculator does it with the sun data for Pakistani cities.

faq.q: How much does a solar system cost in Pakistan?
faq.a: It depends on the size, and larger systems cost less per watt. The solar system price page gives dated ranges for common sizes, and the solar price tracker shows how they have moved.

Not for new connections, which are on net billing: imports are billed at the slab rate and exports bought at a flat buyback rate far below it. Agreements signed before 9 February 2026 keep the old terms until they expire.

On-grid has the shorter payback where the supply is reliable; hybrid adds a battery for loadshedding at a higher price. The Home Power Planner compares both, and backup without solar, for your own home.

key_facts: Solar system size in kW = units used a day ÷ the units one kW of solar makes a day in the city; 15.8 units a day in Lahore needs 3.95 kW, installed as 7 panels of 585 W.

Under net billing the imported units are billed at the normal slab rate (Rs 36.46 per unit for 400 units) and exported units are bought back at a flat rate, Rs 8.13 per unit, NEPRA's national average energy purchase price for CY 2026.
Price per watt = total quoted price ÷ (system kW × one thousand); it is the only fair way to compare quotes of different sizes.
